Ugh, same issue — `-a` is valid too. I keep confusing myself. Let me just replace those two entries with genuinely invalid names: 'a-b ' (trailing space is a value issue... no, name with trailing space) — 'a b' already covers space. Let me use 'a!' (valid!) hmm.

Invalid names: anything with a char outside [a-z0-9!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~]. E.g. 'a,', 'a;', 'a:', 'a=', 'a?', 'a@', 'a[', 'a"', 'a<', 'a{', 'a(', 'a)', 'a\\', 'a\t', 'a\n', '' (empty), 'A'.

Let me use 'a?' and 'a;' in place of '-a' and '.a'. Wait 'a,b' and 'a;b' are already in the list. Let me use 'a?' and 'a:'.

arguments.command: cd /workspace/tmp && sed -i "164s|'-a','.a','']:|'a?b','.a.b;','']:|" t2.py && sed -n '164p' t2.py && cd /workspace && python3 tmp/t2.py 2>&1 | tail -12
